priority.text: The exemption was written in 1967 for a bank stuck with a building it never wanted, and for decades it mostly covered homes. priority.section: Proposition 43 – Increased Threshold for Special Taxes, State Measure
priority.text: Prop 43 would require a two-thirds vote to pass, extend or raise local special taxes proposed by citizen petition, and would ban new local property taxes based on a property’s value. The Chamber is in support of Prop 43 because the California Supreme Court’s Upland ruling has created an unevenly applied system where government qualified ballot measures require 3 voter approval but signature gathering efforts only require 50%. The Chamber believes this runs contrary to the intent of the California constitution’s requirement that special tax measures require 3 approval.

priority.text: Prop A is a common-sense solution to an obvious problem: City Hall has too much bureaucracy that slows everything down. The ultimate Directly Responsible Individual is the Mayor, and voters decide if he or she has done a good job. But currently the Mayor lacks the power to hold individuals accountable in many departments because they are shielded by commissions that don't answer to the Mayor.
